EX-99.1 2 tm2629434d1_ex99-1.htm EXHIBIT 99.1 Exhibit 99.1 Ocugen and Celairis Therapeutics Enter into Exclusive License Agreement for OCU400 in Australia, New Zealand, and ASEAN · Celairis receives exclusive rights to commercialize OCU400, Ocugen's investigational modifier gene therapy for retinitis pigmentosa (RP), in Australia, New Zealand, and member states of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) markets · Expands access to a potential one-time treatment gene therapy for RP across a region with an estimated 725 million people, following potential OCU400 approval in the U.S. · Ocugen receives an upfront license fee, potential development and milestone payments totaling up to $7.1 million, including $6.1 million associated with the upfront payment and OCU400 top-line results (expected in the first quarter of 2027), a high single-digit percentage royalty on net sales, and 50% of gross profits from OCU400 net sales across the region · Celairis will be responsible for regional regulatory submissions, market access, and commercialization of OCU400 across the region MALVERN, Pa., and SYDNEY, Nov. 10, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Ocugen, Inc.

Under the terms of the License Agreement, Ocugen will receive an upfront license fee, as well as potential development and milestone payments totaling up to $7.1 million, including $6.1 million associated with the upfront payment and OCU400 top-line results (expected in the first quarter of 2027), a high single-digit percentage royalty on net sales, and 50% of gross profits from OCU400 net sales in the Territory.

Ocugen is conducting the Phase 3 liMeliGhT clinical trial of OCU400, with topline data expected in the first quarter of 2027, followed by planned global regulatory submissions, including a Biologics License Application in the U.S. and a Marketing Authorization Application in Europe.
